Share on X Telegram The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has indicated that it is considering an increase in the monthly upkeep allowance paid to students under the federal government’s student loan scheme.
The fund’s managing director, Akin Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines, hosted by Nifemi Oguntoye on TVC News on Friday.
NELFUND currently pays eligible students ₦20,000 monthly to support their living expenses. However, the allowance has come under scrutiny amid rising costs of food, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities.
Speaking on the possibility of reviewing the amount, Sawyer said the allowance was under constant consideration, noting that the fund was open to adjustments.
“Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said.
He explained that any proposed increase would depend on the fund’s financial capacity to sustain payments to all beneficiaries without compromising its other obligations.
According to him, NELFUND must carefully plan any adjustment to ensure that it can continue catering for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme.
“What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said.
The NELFUND chief also disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention to improve the financial support available to students.
Although he did not provide details of the proposed intervention, Sawyer said the President was interested in ensuring that students received more meaningful financial assistance to enable them to complete their academic programmes.
“I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said.
He further hinted that changes to the existing arrangement could be announced in the future.
“I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added.
The possible review comes amid growing concerns over the adequacy of the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance, as students contend with the increasing cost of basic living expenses.
The upkeep allowance is one of the components of the Federal Government’s student loan scheme, which provides financial assistance to eligible students in public tertiary institutions for tuition fees and living expenses.
NELFUND said it had disbursed ₦180.5billion to students as upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024.
The fund also disclosed that it had paid ₦194.7billion to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees, bringing its total disbursements to approximately ₦375.2billion.
It added that it had received more than 2.5 million applications and recorded about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions.
However, Sawyer did not announce a new allowance amount or provide a timeline for the implementation of any increase.
